title: How Long Does Hardwood Floor Installation Take? A Realistic Timeline
meta: Hardwood floor installation takes 2 to 4 days for prefinished and 7 to 10 for site-finished on an Everett main floor. Day-by-day timeline from Wills Flooring.
keywords: how long does hardwood floor installation take, hardwood flooring installation time, how many days to install hardwood floors, hardwood floor installation timeline, hardwood installation Everett WA
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Prefinished hardwood on a typical 800 to 1,200 sq ft Everett main floor takes 2 to 4 working days to install. Unfinished, site-finished hardwood takes 7 to 10 days because sanding and three coats of finish follow the install.
blocks.detail: Add 3 to 7 days of acclimation before either one starts, a day for tear-out if old flooring is coming up, and a day for a staircase. Wills Flooring installs prefinished at $3.25 per sq ft and unfinished at $2.75 per sq ft.

blocks.html: The honest answer to "how long will this take" has two parts, and most quotes only give you one. There is the time a crew is in your house making noise, and there is the total calendar time from the day the wood is delivered to the day the couch goes back. For a Boeing family in Silver Lake trying to plan around shift schedules, or a Port Gardner condo owner with a building work window, the second number is the one that matters. Here is both, day by day, based on how our crews actually run jobs in Everett.

blocks.text: Day by day: a 1,000 sq ft prefinished install

items.text: Boxes arrive and sit open in the rooms where they will be installed, at normal living temperature. Engineered needs about 3 days; solid oak needs 5 to 7, longer in a wet Everett winter. Nothing else happens yet.

Old carpet, pad, staples and tack strip come up, or old laminate is pulled. We check the subfloor for squeaks, high spots and moisture, screw down loose sheets and grind or fill as needed. In a 1920s Riverside house this can take the whole day; in a 1990s Eastmont home it is often half.

A two-person crew lays roughly 300 to 500 sq ft of straight-lay prefinished plank per day, including cuts around cabinets and closets. Racking boards for color mix, nailing or gluing, and fitting under door jambs are what eat the hours. Diagonal or herringbone patterns cut that pace nearly in half.

Quarter round or base shoe goes back on, transitions to tile and carpet are set, and vents are fitted. Furniture can go back the same evening on a nailed prefinished floor; glued floors need 24 hours before heavy loads.

blocks.text: What speeds a job up and what slows it down

items.title: The age of the house
items.text: Riverside and Bayside homes from the 1900s to 1920s almost always need subfloor work: sistered joists, shimmed low spots, sometimes a new plywood layer over old plank subfloor. Silver Lake and Eastmont houses from the 1990s and 2000s usually have flat OSB or plywood and go faster by a day.

items.title: Room shape and cuts
items.text: Every doorway, closet, angled wall and cabinet toe-kick is a set of hand cuts. An open rectangular living room installs at the fast end of the range. A chopped-up floor plan with five bedrooms and two halls installs at the slow end even at the same square footage.

items.title: Pattern and plank width
items.text: Wide planks cover ground faster than 2¼ in strip. Herringbone, chevron and diagonal layouts roughly double the cutting and layout time. Mixed widths and long European planks need more careful racking so the joints look random, and that sorting happens before a single board is nailed.

items.title: Building access and scheduling
items.text: Port Gardner and downtown Everett condos limit work hours and elevator use, which can turn a two-day job into three. Our showroom is about 15 minutes away in Lynnwood, so material and crew logistics are simple; the building rules are usually the constraint.

blocks.title: Do not skip acclimation to save days:
blocks.text: Solid hardwood installed straight off a cold delivery truck in an Everett winter will gap when the furnace dries it out, or cup if the house is more humid than the boxes were. Acclimation is dead time on the calendar, but it is the cheapest insurance the job has. We drop the wood off early so the clock starts before the crew arrives.
How to keep your install on schedule

items.html: Clear the rooms before the crew arrives. Every hour spent moving furniture is an hour not laying floor. Empty closets too; they are the slowest square footage in the house.
Run the house at normal living conditions. Heat on, windows closed, humidity where it will be when you live there. Acclimating wood to a cold empty house then warming it up defeats the purpose.
Settle transitions and trim decisions early. Whether quarter round is painted, whether the tile threshold stays: these decisions made on day three cost a return trip.
Sequence the other trades. Painters should finish walls before the floor and come back for base trim after. Cabinets go in before hardwood in most kitchens, appliances after.
Ask for a written schedule with the quote. Our hardwood installation quotes list the days, the acclimation period and the cure times, and are backed by a 1-year workmanship warranty.

faq.q: How long does it take to install 1,000 square feet of hardwood?
faq.a: Two to three working days for prefinished plank in a straight lay, after 3 to 7 days of acclimation. Site-finished unfinished hardwood takes about seven to eight days: the same install time, then a day or two of sanding and three to four days for three coats of finish to be applied and dry.

faq.q: How long does hardwood need to acclimate before installation?
faq.a: Engineered hardwood needs about 3 days in the rooms where it will be installed. Solid hardwood needs 5 to 7 days, and in a damp Everett winter we sometimes wait longer until a moisture meter shows the boards within a couple of points of the subfloor. Skipping this step causes most gapping and cupping complaints.

faq.q: Can I stay in the house during hardwood installation?
faq.a: Yes for prefinished. The work is loud during the day but there is no finish odor and rooms are usable each evening. For site-finished floors you need to stay off the finished area for 24 hours after each coat and keep pets away, so many families leave for the final finishing days.

faq.q: How long before I can walk on new hardwood floors?
faq.a: Nailed prefinished floors can be walked on as soon as the crew is done. Glued floors need about 24 hours before heavy foot traffic and furniture. Site-finished floors can take socks after 24 hours, shoes after 48, furniture after 72 hours, and rugs after about two weeks while the finish fully cures.

faq.q: Does installing hardwood on stairs add much time?
faq.a: A straight run of 13 treads with risers takes about one full day for an experienced installer, at $125 per stair. Open-sided stairs with returns, landings and pie-shaped treads take longer because each piece is scribed and fitted by hand. We usually schedule stairs as the last day of the job.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to get hardwood installed in Everett?
faq.a: Choose an in-stock prefinished engineered plank, clear the rooms yourself and book off-season. Engineered acclimates in about 3 days, installs quickly and needs no finishing. Wills Flooring's showroom is roughly 15 minutes from most of Everett, so samples, measuring and a firm quote can happen within a few days of your call.
